channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Começa a valer lei que autoriza venda de spray de pimenta para mulheres; veja regras
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva signed a law authorizing the sale and possession of pepper spray for women over 18 as a self-defense measure, vetoing the original proposal that allowed use from age 16 with parental consent. The law sets strict purchase requirements, including photo ID, proof of residence, and a clean criminal record, limits containers to 50 ml, and mandates use only in response to an unjust, current, or imminent threat, with immediate discontinuation after the threat is neutralized.

item.title: PL vai ao TSE para barrar divulgação de documentário sobre Flávio
item.description: The Liberal Party (PL) has filed a request with the TSE to block the dissemination of a documentary produced by Instituto Conhecimento Liberta (ICL) about Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, claiming it constitutes illegal pre-campaign negative propaganda financed by a legal entity. The PL argues the material violates electoral law by promoting unfavorable content against the presidential pre-candidate without proper authorization or opposing view.

item.title: MPF arquiva denúncia do Psol contra Tarcísio de Freitas sobre elo com PCC
item.description: The Federal Public Ministry (MPF) archived a complaint filed by Psol against São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas, alleging a link to the PCC through an electoral donation from a businesswoman allegedly tied to the criminal group in 2022. The decision cited lack of concrete evidence connecting the donation to organized crime and no indication of the governor’s knowledge, participation, omission, or facilitation. The archiving followed a review of an appeal against an earlier dismissal by the Regional Electoral Prosecutor’s Office.

item.title: No AP, Lula lidera 1º turno, mas empata tecnicamente com Flávio no 2º, aponta RealTime/Big Data
item.description: A RealTime/Big Data poll released on Friday shows Lula leading with 36% in first-round voting intentions for the Brazilian presidential election in Amapá, followed by Flávio Bolsonaro at 31%. In a hypothetical runoff, the two are technically tied, indicating a closely contested race in the state. Other candidates received significantly lower percentages.

item.title: Dois vídeos e um acordo: a "paz" de Flávio e Michelle
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro released a video publicly apologizing to Michelle Bolsonaro for family disagreements, admitting faults and calling for unity among supporters. Michelle responded by accepting the apology but emphasized her work with PL Mulher and credited Celina Leão and Damares Alves for facilitating the reconciliation, which occurred just before the PL convention that will formalize his presidential pre-candidacy. The apparent truce is seen as a backroom political move, reflecting Flávio’s electoral isolation due to lack of Centrón support and no running mate.

item.title: Reina a paz entre Flávio e sua madrasta, até a próxima briga
item.description: Under pressure, Flávio Bolsonaro apologized to his stepmother Michelle Bolsonaro after she accused him of emotionally stabbing her. He had previously denied mistreating or humiliating her. Michelle forgave him, restoring peace — at least until the next family clash.

item.title: Análise: Michelle pode faltar à convenção, mas 'acordo de paz' dá fôlego a Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro is struggling to secure key political alliances due to family rifts and investigations involving Daniel Vorcaro and Banco Master. To counter the perception of a fractured campaign, PL president Valdemar Costa Neto brokered a 'peace agreement' with Michelle Bolsonaro, contingent on a public apology from Flávio, which he delivered. Although Michelle is not expected to attend the PL's national convention on May 25, she may send a supportive video, which could help project unity and bolster Flávio's efforts to gain allies.

item.title: A disputa entre Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro no Amapá, segundo o Real Time Big Data
item.description: Lula leads the presidential race in Amapá with 36% voting intentions in the first round, while Flávio Bolsonaro has 31%. In the second round, there is a technical tie: Flávio at 44% and Lula at 42%, within the two-point margin of error. The Real Time Big Data survey interviewed 1,600 people between July 19 and 23.

item.title: Tarcísio diz que Trivia Trens poderá perder concessão de 3 linhas
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas stated that Trivia Trens may lose the concession for lines 11-Coral, 12-Safira, and 13-Jade if it fails to meet contractual obligations, following a train fire on line 12-Safira due to a short circuit. He criticized the company for persistent operational issues since the start of its concession, calling them 'unacceptable'. CPTM has temporarily resumed joint operations with the concessionaire for 90 days, as ordered by Artesp, to investigate causes and prevent further disruptions.

item.title: Após um mês de crise, Michelle e Flávio Bolsonaro devem gravar vídeo juntos
item.description: Michelle and Flávio Bolsonaro are set to record a joint video to end a one-month dispute stemming from disagreements over PL party articulations in Ceará. The video will be the final step in a three-stage strategy: Flávio's apology, Michelle's response, and then their joint appearance to publicly show reconciliation. The goal is to halt the loss of female and conservative voter support in Flávio's presidential pre-campaign, following a poll showing 42% of respondents sided with Michelle in the conflict.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro rebate críticas sobre vídeo de preços no mercado
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro released a video defending his supermarket price comparison, claiming the left is upset for exposing Brazil's rising cost of living. He urged followers to film prices of basic goods and blamed the increase on Lula's government and the 15% Selic rate, despite using 2019 data as a reference — a choice criticized for ignoring post-pandemic inflation.

item.title: Crusoé: Enrolado Master
item.description: The Liberal Party (PL) national convention to confirm Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential candidacy is scheduled for this Saturday, the 25th, in São Paulo. The event will feature Argentine President Javier Milei and São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas. Despite institutional backing, Flávio Bolsonaro is reportedly in a delicate situation ahead of the convention, as suggested by the headline 'Enrolled Master'.

item.title: A estratégia de Flávio por trás do pedido de desculpas a Michelle Bolsonaro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's apology to Michelle Bolsonaro was a calculated move to win Centrão support and lower his electoral rejection, strengthening his 2026 presidential pre-candidacy.

item.title: ‘Minha Casa, Minha Vida’ chega a novo recorde no atual mandato de Lula
item.description: The Minha Casa, Minha Vida program reached 2.5 million contracted housing units during Lula's third term, according to the Ministry of Cities. Minister Antônio Vladimir Moura Lima stated the goal of 3 million units by year-end remains achievable, with the Southeast and Northeast regions leading in allocations.

item.title: Pesquisas eleitorais: saiba quais levantamentos podem sair nesta 6ª
item.description: Electoral polls registered with the TSE were cleared for publication on Friday, July 24, 2026, covering the presidential race and regional elections in Amapá, Amazonas, Goiás, Mato Grosso do Sul, and Sergipe. The surveys comply with electoral transparency laws and were released by Poder360, which offers its Poll Aggregator to Drive subscribers.

item.title: Governo Lula: leia a agenda de ministros nesta 6ª feira
item.description: On Friday (July 24, 2026), the Lula government's agenda focuses on fiscal data disclosure, science and education, labor relations, and international affairs. The highlight is the presentation of the RARDP for the third quarter by the Ministry of Planning at 3:00 p.m. Meanwhile, the Education and Science ministers meet with Lula and SBPC leaders in São Paulo, while the Labor Minister discusses the 6x1 work schedule with unions. Agendas for 33 of the 38 ministers were not disclosed.

item.title: 52% preferem Brasil mais próximo da China e não dos EUA
item.description: 52% of Brazilian voters prefer Brazil to strengthen commercial ties with China over the United States, according to a PoderData survey from July 2024, while 35% favor the U.S. This reverses the 2025 trend, when 59% preferred the U.S. The decline in U.S. image among Brazilians, tied to Donald Trump’s policies and his alliance with Bolsonaro, explains the shift.

item.title: SobeDesce: da Vale ao Corinthians
item.description: The content highlights Vale's record iron ore production, Kylian Mbappé's goal-scoring records across major tournaments, the global box office success of Christopher Nolan's 'Odyssey', criticism of Daniel Ortega's move to cancel elections in Nicaragua, a decline in Brazilian mergers and acquisitions, and Corinthians receiving a transfer ban for unpaid dues to Midtjylland. No Brazilian 2026 election candidates are mentioned.

item.title: Direita aposta no antipetismo para enfrentar favoritismo de Lula na eleição
item.description: The Brazilian right is banking on anti-PT sentiment as its core strategy to challenge Lula’s frontrunner status in the 2026 election, leveraging persistent PT rejection rates of 36% to 42% according to Genial/Quaest. Despite Lula’s recovery driven by R$200 billion in social spending and opposition disarray, anti-PT sentiment — fueled by the denial of scandals like the mensalão and Operation Car Wash — remains a decisive obstacle in an election likely to be decided by a narrow margin, as in 2022.

item.title: Embates de poder: uma disputa por protagonismo no coração da corrida eleitoral
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes ordered an electoral police investigation into Senator Flávio Bolsonaro for alleged premature campaigning after he shared a letter from Jair Bolsonaro praising him as Brazil’s best option to fight corruption and poverty. Moraes barred Flávio from visiting his father and suggested revising Jair Bolsonaro’s house arrest, sparking debate over STF overreach into electoral matters traditionally handled by the TSE. Though the penalty is minor, the move signals growing tension between the two courts over electoral oversight and political influence.

item.title: Arminio Fraga: “O quadro é desastroso”
item.description: Arminio Fraga, former Central Bank president and respected economist, warns of a disastrous economic outlook for Brazil, citing over 80 million indebted individuals, corporate difficulties in rolling over debt, and the government shortening its debt profile as clear signs of impending recession. He criticizes the Lula administration for failing to curb debt growth despite austerity claims, noting that the fiscal framework has been breached and high long-term interest rates reflect a loss of market confidence, not just cyclical inflation pressures. Fraga argues that without significantly higher investment and productivity gains, Brazil cannot achieve sustainable growth, maintaining a mediocre per capita growth rate of just 1.3% since 1994.

item.title: Bloqueio de verbas das agências reguladoras suspende investimentos vitais para o país
item.description: The blocking of 382 million reais in funding for Brazilian regulatory agencies, authorized by the Lula government in May, is undermining vital investments for economic development and national security. The measure directly impacted ANM, which suspended the auction of strategic mineral areas critical for the energy transition, and halted on-site inspections of tailings dams, increasing the risk of new disasters like Mariana and Brumadinho. Anvisa also faces constraints in its oversight activities, endangering public health.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro segue estratégia de radicalização, diz autor de ação que tornou ex-presidente inelegível
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, senator and PL presidential candidate, is accused of committing an electoral crime by questioning the integrity of Brazil’s electronic voting machines and spreading false information to foreign diplomats, according to Walber Agra, the lawyer behind the action that made Jair Bolsonaro ineligible. The incident took place in Brasília on Tuesday (21), echoing the 2022 meeting with ambassadors at the Alvorada Palace that led to the former president’s disqualification.

item.title: Derrete ou não?
item.description: The poll shows that 66.2% of readers believe Flávio Bolsonaro's candidacy will collapse before the end, while 33.8% think it will last until the finish. The content also includes a cartoon by Aroeira criticizing the Bolsonaros as coup plotters and references other blog articles.

item.title: Para 50%, idade de Lula não é um problema para a reeleição
item.description: Half of voters (50%) say that President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's age of 80 would not be a problem for a potential reelection in 2026, according to a PoderData survey from July. This represents a 24-point increase since July 2025. Despite public slips, medical procedures, and comparisons to Joe Biden, 43% still view his age as a negative factor, while 7% were undecided.

item.title: Baixa no PT da Bahia fortalece campanha de Benedita no Rio
item.description: The campaign of federal deputy Benedita da Silva (PT-RJ) for the Federal Senate gained momentum with the hiring of Marcus Di Flora, former Communications Secretary of the Bahia government, to lead her communication strategy. Benedita’s candidacy is a national PT priority, aiming to strengthen the party’s Senate bloc and support President Lula’s electoral base in Rio de Janeiro. She previously served as Rio’s governor and minister in Lula’s first administration, though she resigned in 2004 over allegations of misusing public funds for religious trips abroad.

item.title: Com eleições e recorde de emendas, apoio a Lula recua no Congresso, mostra levantamento
item.description: Support for President Lula’s government in Congress has sharply declined, with governability dropping from 75% to 38.5% in the Senate and from 58% to 38.1% in the Chamber of Deputies in the first half of 2025. This decline is driven by growing distance from Centrão parties and a record surge in parliamentary amendments—totaling R$33.89 billion by July 4—increasing legislative independence and complicating the passage of key reforms like the 6x1 workweek PEC.

item.title: A desigualdade racial que o voto eleitoral não corrige
item.description: The article analyzes the persistent racial inequality in access to power positions within the Brazilian Chamber of Deputies, even after the election of Black deputies. Despite affirmative measures that increased Black representation in electoral contests, white parliamentarians continue to exhibit higher parliamentary professionalization, measured by the Parliamentary Professionalization Index (IPP), granting them greater control over committee presidencies and rapporteurships, thereby reproducing an internal power hierarchy that electoral outcomes do not correct.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro está isolado após sucessão de crises na campanha à Presidência?
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro officially launches his presidential campaign amid political isolation, lacking party alliances and a running mate, while facing internal crises including public clashes with Michelle Bolsonaro and ties to the Banco Master scandal. His public apology to Michelle, viewed as a symbolic move to appeal to female and evangelical voters, has not yet secured backing from key parties like União Progressista and Republicanos, which remain neutral. His campaign struggles to gain traction among women, the majority of the electorate, as he attempts to reposition himself as a moderate candidate.

item.title: Master: PT retoma ofensiva a Flávio após inquérito sobre Dark Horse
item.description: The PT intensified attacks against Flávio Bolsonaro after the Federal Police were authorized to investigate a R$ 61 million transfer from banker Daniel Vorcaro for the film Dark Horse, linked to Jair Bolsonaro. Deputy Lindbergh Farias noted Flávio promised to disclose the funds' use within a month but has not done so, while Flávio’s campaign denies any wrongdoing. The case resurfaces ahead of the PL convention that will formally nominate him as presidential candidate.

item.title: Caso Master volta a gerar preocupação nos aliados de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Supreme Court Justice André Mendonça authorized an investigation into banker Daniel Vorcaro’s financial transfers to the film Dark Horse, linked to Flávio Bolsonaro. The probe, requested by the Federal Police with support from the Attorney General’s Office, examines approximately R$ 61 million sent to a U.S.-based fund tied to allies of former president Jair Bolsonaro. Flávio Bolsonaro’s allies fear the case could become a 'Pandora’s box,' uncovering further financial ties and damaging his 2026 presidential pre-candidacy.

item.title: Convenção e Caso Master levaram Flávio a pedir desculpas a Michelle
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro issued a public apology to Michelle Bolsonaro to ease family tensions ahead of the PL convention that will officially nominate him as a presidential candidate on July 25 in São Paulo. The move also aimed to counterbalance negative publicity from the ongoing 'Caso Master' scandal, which had been damaging his public image.

item.title: Filho de golpista, golpista é. Os Bolsonaros são prova disso
item.description: Jair Bolsonaro's sons, Flávio and Eduardo, renewed attacks on Brazil's electoral system and ministers of the TSE and STF, accusing them of persecuting their father, mirroring his own coup-plotting behavior. Michelle Bolsonaro, despite publicly praising the judiciary, allegedly encouraged Jair to carry out the failed coup, according to former aide Mauro Cid, and her video attacking Flávio was not a coordinated move, as she emerged as a victim of family abuse. The text argues the Bolsonaro family reproduces Jair's authoritarian and coup-oriented conduct, with Michelle attempting to preserve her image as a 'good wife' amid familial decline.

item.title: A resistência de Carlos Bolsonaro na trégua entre Flávio e Michelle
item.description: The effort to persuade Flávio Bolsonaro to record a public apology to Michelle Bolsonaro proved difficult, largely due to resistance from Carlos Bolsonaro. The process was described as arduous, with Carlos acting as a key obstacle to familial reconciliation within the Bolsonaro clan. The subscriber-exclusive article highlights internal tensions among Bolsonaro family members amid reports of a tentative truce.

item.title: Tarcísio e Haddad apostam em propostas de combate à violência para mobilizar eleitores de SP
item.description: Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) and Fernando Haddad (PT) are betting on public security as a central theme to mobilize voters in São Paulo, with the governor highlighting actions like the end of Cracolândia and the Muralha Paulista program, while the former minister prepares to unveil his security plan next week. Both pre-candidates see security as the state's main problem, according to a Quaest poll, and are structuring their government plans with technical teams and security-focused agendas, aiming for registration by August 15.

item.title: Celina ajudou a elaborar roteiro dos vídeos de Flavio e Michelle
item.description: Distrito Federal Governor Celina Leão (PP) played a key behind-the-scenes role in reconciling Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) and former First Lady Michelle Bolsonaro (PL), assisting in negotiations and helping draft and review the scripts for their apology and acceptance videos shared on social media. Michelle publicly thanked Celina Leão and former Minister Damares Alves for their efforts in achieving family reconciliation, which followed a period of tension after Flávio's public remarks downplayed Michelle's role in the right-wing political articulation.

item.title: Missão lança ex-funkeiro do Bonde do Rolê a deputado federal no Paraná
item.description: Pedro Deyrot, a former funk musician from Bonde do Rolê and MBL activist, has been officially nominated as a federal deputy candidate for the Mission Party in Paraná. His background spans international music, tomato farming, and political activism, with fiscal responsibility and spending cuts as his central campaign platform.

item.title: Do 'perdão' à maquiagem e escolha da roupa: os bastidores dos vídeos que selaram a reconciliação entre Flávio e Michelle Bolsonaro
item.description: The video in which Flávio Bolsonaro apologized to Michelle Bolsonaro was the result of delicate negotiations, with initial resistance from the senator to using the word 'forgiveness'. Michelle, meanwhile, had already prepared her response, carefully choosing a white blouse and filming at an external location (a nearby bakery) to avoid violating the social media restrictions imposed on former President Jair Bolsonaro by the STF. Her strategy included visual symbolism, repeating a tactic of communicating through elements like color and setting, previously used in her public manifestations.

item.title: Os próximos passos da reconciliação de Flávio e Michelle Bolsonaro
item.description: Allies of Flávio and Michelle Bolsonaro are working behind the scenes to arrange an in-person meeting and record a new video featuring the former first lady, to be aired at the PL’s national convention this Saturday (25). The goal is to publicly overcome the family rift and solidify Flávio’s 2026 presidential candidacy. While the virtual reconciliation was celebrated by Bolsonaro’s base, the focus now is turning the gesture into a coordinated political move.

item.title: Paz na família? Entenda reconciliação entre Flávio e Michelle em meio a 'momento difícil' da campanha
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro released a video apologizing to his stepmother Michelle Bolsonaro after a public dispute that damaged his image, particularly among female voters. Michelle responded by thanking him and forgiving him, signaling a family reconciliation amid the challenges of the 2026 presidential campaign.

item.title: Crise na campanha de Flávio abre brechas, e candidatos da direita ampliam ataques em busca de deserções no bolsonarismo
item.description: The crisis in Flávio Bolsonaro’s campaign has weakened his support among right-wing voters who do not identify as Bolsonaristas, dropping from 74% to 54% in voter intentions. His rivals — Ronaldo Caiado, Romeu Zema, and Renan Santos — are exploiting this vulnerability, intensifying public attacks and strategic agendas with sectors like agribusiness, business leaders, and religious figures, aiming to lure defections from Bolsonarism.

item.title: No PL, aliados classificam articulação de Flávio com Centrão como 'tragédia' e já admitem candidatura avulsa
item.description: PL leaders describe Flávio Bolsonaro's political articulation with the Centrão as a 'tragedy', as he entered the campaign without national alliances after the União Progressista federation declared neutrality. The campaign failed by neglecting daily relations with party leaders, including a gesture seen as abandonment during the operation against Ciro Nogueira, and now considers a 'solo' candidacy supported solely by the PL's structure.

item.title: Gestão Tarcísio indicou diretor de Fundação ABC investigada pelo MPSP
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas admitted he appointed physician Aldemir Humberto Soares to lead the ABC Foundation after a disagreement among ABC municipalities over the presidency rotation. Soares, then state health secretary coordinator, opened the public bidding that resulted in FUABC being contracted to manage health professionals at Emilio Ribas Hospital — a contract now under investigation by the São Paulo MP for potential irregularities. The case is cited as a key episode in the MPSC’s lawsuit seeking to terminate the outsourcing agreement.

item.title: Gayer pede que Mauro Vieira explique posição do Brasil sobre Venezuela
item.description: Federal deputy Gustavo Gayer (PL-GO) requested the summoning of Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira to clarify Brazil's foreign policy toward Venezuela, citing allegations of electoral fraud linked to Smartmatic voting machines and a CIA report on Venezuelan election manipulation. Although Brazil does not use Smartmatic machines, Gayer and allies associated the country with fraud suspicions, also demanding explanations on the reimbursement of Venezuela's debts covered by Brazil's National Treasury. The request aims to define Itamaraty's stance amid Venezuela's institutional crisis and the 2024 presidential elections.

item.title: Por que Flávio questiona as urnas?
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro questioned the reliability of Brazil's electronic voting machines during an event with foreign diplomats last Tuesday, repeating arguments similar to those used by his father, Jair Bolsonaro, in July 2022, when he also invited ambassadors to attack the electoral system.

item.title: Autofagia eleitoral bolsonarista
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, son of former President Jair Bolsonaro and the PL party's presidential candidate for 2026, has seen his campaign deteriorate over recent months due to controversies, including the revelation of a multi-million reais contribution from Daniel Vorcaro to a biopic about his father, alongside strategic missteps. These developments have turned him into a politically toxic option ahead of the party convention that will formally nominate him, prompting the question: who would actually benefit from his potential victory in October?

item.title: Daniel Ortega escancarou nova ditadura familiar na Nicarágua
item.description: Daniel Ortega announced there will be no more elections in Nicaragua, cementing a family dictatorship by appointing his wife, Rosario Murillo, as 'co-president'. After years of repression, censorship, and jailing of opponents, the former Sandinista hero now replicates the authoritarianism he once fought, according to critics like Frei Betto. Lula, who once supported the revolution, saw his plea for the release of an imprisoned bishop ignored, marking the definitive end of diplomatic relations with Brazil.

item.title: Governo age para afastar centrão de Flávio Bolsonaro, e Lula deve poupar Ciro Nogueira na campanha
item.description: The Lula government is working to distance the centrão from Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, aiming to isolate his main rival in the 2026 presidential race. Plenary emissaries have engaged with the leadership of Republicans, Brazil Union, and PP, with the latter already informing Flávio it will remain neutral in the contest. The strategy seeks to weaken the senator’s political and electoral backing in Rio de Janeiro.

item.title: EUA deixam 2.000 produtos sem tarifa dupla, diz governo Lula
item.description: Minister Márcio Elias Rosa stated that approximately 2,000 Brazilian products exported to the U.S. will not face double taxation, remaining subject only to the new U.S. tariff of 12.5%. Sectors such as machinery, auto parts, and textiles will face a cumulative tariff of 37.5%, while products like beef, coffee, and orange juice will only incur the 12.5% rate. The Brazilian government rejects the measure and seeks diplomatic negotiation for its removal, reserving the right to respond under the Economic Reciprocity Law.

item.title: Inquérito sobre 'Dark Horse' vai apurar corrupção e lavagem e mirar Flávio, Eduardo e Vorcaro
item.description: An investigation has been opened into alleged crimes of currency evasion, money laundering, and corruption tied to financial transfers from Daniel Vorcaro to the film 'Dark Horse,' which depicts the life of former President Jair Bolsonaro. The probe specifically targets Flávio Bolsonaro, Eduardo Bolsonaro, and Daniel Vorcaro, who are suspected of involvement in the financial scheme behind the movie's production.
